caveats: Conflicts surface as GitHub merge conflicts (94 of 191 open PRs CONFLICTING); Cuenca does not resolve or rebase them, and that was not exercised.
Every landing opened its own PR (179 in the hour), the behaviour BRO-3501 changes.
in_journal_not_acknowledged (75 Mac, 20 NUC) are drafts from the smoke run, probes and A/B run on soak-mac-00/01 and soak-nuc-15/16 before the hour; no other fork has any.
The harness kept only stderr; in --json mode the CLI prints errors to stdout, so failure messages would have been dropped. No snapshot or landing failed in the hour.

In the 2-minute smoke run before the hour, 4 of 5 Mac edits were not readable over SMB within 60 s while the NUC volume had them in ~1 s. Not reproduced in an A/B run with Samba oplocks on and off (30/30 each) nor in the 3,483 Mac edits measured here (0 missed). Cause unknown; BRO-3521.
Readers: 15 polling threads on one Mac mount plus the NUC watcher; no second device.

soak.py is committed exactly as it ran. Its chaos step does not check the return codes of gh or of the ssh kill, and run() keeps only stderr. Both outcomes those gaps could have hidden were confirmed independently. The restart: systemd NRestarts=2 (smoke kill plus this one), and 4 NUC snapshots offline at 05:25:11-12Z. The skipped merges: every open conflict.txt PR is CONFLICTING in soak-nuc-prs.json. A rerun should fix both in the harness first.
audit: per fork: each acknowledged id must appear exactly once in its own fork's draft_published records; ids in two forks counted (0); mutation-tested (an id moved to another fork's journal reads as lost 1)

commands.nuc_agents: sudo systemd-run --unit soak-nuc --uid=agent --setenv=HOME=/home/agent --setenv=CUENCA_BIN=/usr/local/bin/cuenca python3 /opt/soak/soak.py agent --side nuc --names /home/agent/soak/names.txt --root /home/agent/soak/run --out /home/agent/soak/out/main --seconds 3600 --land-every 40 --req /tmp/soak-vis/req-main.jsonl --res /tmp/soak-vis-res/res-main.jsonl
